rules.notes: Single source of truth for tag + collection rules and the approved tag catalog. Read by zotero-semantic-tagger, zotero-library-curator and their lint scripts. No markdown mirror is maintained.

prefixes.boundary: Workflow/status of MY reading or work on the paper (`_to-read`, `_reading`, `_key-paper`, `_implement`).

Research methodologies, experimental assays, and computational/statistical techniques, tasks or analyses APPLIED BY THE INVESTIGATOR; scoring/mathematical functions (`met:scoring-function`). Never a natural biophysical/biological phenomenon.
prefixes.excludes: ML architectures (`ml:`), runnable software (`tool:`), natural processes (`proc:`).

prefixes.boundary: Machine-learning or statistical model families, architectures, objectives, interpretation techniques (`ml:cnn`, `ml:gradient-boosting`).
prefixes.excludes: The task it solves (`met:`), a named runnable product (`tool:`).

prefixes.boundary: Molecular & structural entities: molecules, domains (`bio:rrm`, `bio:dsrbd`), regions (`bio:disordered-region`), chemical modifications at class level (`bio:rna-modification`), macromolecular interactions (`bio:rna-protein-interaction`), targets, pathways, organisms.
prefixes.excludes: Techniques or assays (`met:`), datasets (`data:`), processes (`proc:`), diseases (`dis:`).

prefixes.boundary: Runnable software, library, framework, pipeline or web server a user can execute (`tool:predprba`). Not models or methods merely described in a paper.

Biological and biophysical processes/phenomena that occur in nature (`proc:disorder-to-order-transition`, `proc:phase-separation`, `proc:conformational-change`, `proc:chaperone-folding`, splicing, regulation).
prefixes.excludes: The method used to study it (`met:`), the entity involved (`bio:`).

prefixes.boundary: Translational, engineering or clinical use cases/applications (`app:rna-therapeutics`, `app:aptamer-design`, `app:protein-engineering`, `app:synthetic-biology`).
prefixes.excludes: The design technique itself (`met:rna-design`), a disease (`dis:`).

prefixes.boundary: Diseases, clinical phenotypes or pathological conditions (`dis:cancer`, `dis:autoimmune-disease`, `dis:neurodegenerative-disease`). Class level only.

new_prefix_policy: Strictly orthogonal: captures an attribute none of the active prefixes can express, and no existing tag would need to move into it.
Demonstrated need: applies across at least 5 papers, listed as evidence.
Explicit user confirmation: propose prefix, boundary, examples and the 5+ papers in a table; create nothing until the user says yes. Then update rules.prefixes, rules.regex and this file's consumers.

interaction_rules.note: Exactly these six exist, fixed component order. Tag every interaction type a paper treats. Any bio:*-interaction tag outside the allowed list is an error.

base_tag_rules.rule: Always pair a specific ncRNA subclass (bio:mirna, bio:circrna, bio:lncrna, bio:sirna, ...) with bio:ncrna. Enforced through the catalog 'requires' field.
Stacking requirements: a catalog entry with 'requires' needs those tags on the same item (e.g. met:iclip requires met:clip-seq).

granularity_anti_explosion.rule: Do not create hyper-specific biochemical or molecular subtype tags that would multiply without bound: individual RNA chemical modifications, individual point mutations, single residues, single named genes/proteins used only as an example. Stay at the functional-class level (bio:rna-modification) and compose with class tags (bio:ncrna, bio:mrna, bio:disordered-region). A named entity gets its own tag only when the paper is about that entity as a whole (bio:cas9, bio:pumilio, tool:catrapid).

composition_rules: Orthogonal, atomic tags: one tag = one concept; stack, never compound (bio:rna-protein-interaction + bio:ncrna, NOT bio:ncrna-protein-interaction; met:binding-affinity-prediction + ml:gradient-boosting, NOT met:gradient-boosting-affinity; proc:phase-separation + bio:biomolecular-condensate).

Reuse before invent: merge synonyms into the canonical tag (bio:rna-protein-complex, bio:rna-binding-protein -> bio:rna-protein-interaction; met:binding-site-identification -> met:binding-residue-prediction; met:motif-enrichment -> met:motif-discovery).

met: vs tool:: mathematical/scoring functions, algorithms and techniques are met:; tool: is strictly runnable software, libraries, pipelines or web servers; models only described in a paper are ml:/met:.
No collection duplication: never tag a broad domain a collection name already states.
Legacy tags (topic/..., type/...) are not canonical and have been removed library-wide. zotmoov is ignored (never added, never removed unless asked).
Data provenance tags such as data:wwpdb may be kept despite few text hits when the user flagged (OVERRIDE) and approved them.
Adding a tag to the catalog requires a confirmed write-back. Keep the catalog sorted by prefix, then tag (tools/lint enforce sort).

collections.depth_note: Private_Projects counts as Level 1; a 5th level needs user confirmation.
collections.zotmoov_note: Enabled: the folder tree under pdf_root/Private_Projects mirrors the collection tree; the PDF's parent folder IS the Primary Collection.

todo_deferred: Elephant-1 9B local decision engine (Stage 4): interface still unspecified; only the interactive fallback is active.
Local embedding/reranker tag ranking (bge-m3 + gte-reranker under /srv/ai/registry/weights/embeddings): untested, deferred.
Revisit rule: re-run older collections when a new prefix is promoted.
form_rules: Charset: English, lowercase a-z0-9, single - only; no accents, spaces, / or _ except the leading _ of status tags.
Stopwords: strip a an the of for and in with.
Versions: collapse (tool:alphafold, not tool:alphafold-3) unless the paper benchmarks versions against each other.
Singular for techniques, algorithms, models, molecules, organisms (transformer, rna-seq, crispr-cas9, brca1); plural only for collective categories (bio:biomarkers, data:datasets, ml:embeddings).
Use unambiguous standard acronyms: llm, gwas, pcr, cnn, gnn.
Process vs method vs entity: phenomena are proc:, what the investigator applies is met:, molecules/regions/modifications are bio:.
One concept per tag; pick the prefix by what the thing IS (method vs the tool that implements it); never tag one concept under two prefixes.
Never remove _ status tags unless the user explicitly says so.
Tags never repeat collection or folder names.
rules.data_provenance_override: A low-hit tag that establishes critical experimental vs predicted data provenance (e.g. data:wwpdb) may bypass the Groundedness/hit-count filter ONLY if the proposal table flags it OVERRIDE and the user confirms.

tags.definition: Aptamer design as an application use case. Not the generic design technique (met:rna-design).
tags.components: atomic; pair with met:rna-design or met:feature-extraction

tags.definition: RNA-based therapeutics and vaccines as the motivating or demonstrated application (e.g. designing therapeutic RNA binders). Not the design technique (met:rna-design).
tags.components: atomic; pair with met:rna-design or bio:rna-modification

tags.definition: Synthetic-biology engineering use (designing RNA/protein parts) stated as an application of the work.
tags.components: atomic; pair with a met: design/prediction tag

tags.definition: Biomolecular condensates / membraneless assemblies as an entity. The process of forming them is `proc:phase-separation`.
Cas9 nuclease as a molecular target or component. Not the CRISPR technique.
Intrinsically disordered regions of proteins as a studied entity.
DNA-DNA interactions (e.g. chromatin contacts). Reserved, not yet used.
DNA-protein recognition or binding (canonical order DNA before protein).
The genetic code as a studied entity (codon/amino acid specificity).
Long non-coding RNAs. Always paired with `bio:ncrna`.
RNA or protein chaperones assisting folding.
Messenger RNA as the studied RNA class.
Non-coding RNA as the base category. Required whenever a subclass (`bio:mirna`, `bio:circrna`, `bio:lncrna`, ...) is tagged.
RNA-DNA interactions (e.g. R-loops, lncRNA-chromatin). Reserved, not yet used.
Chemical modifications of RNA as a FUNCTIONAL CLASS (never individual modifications such as m6A or pseudouridine; see granularity rule).
RNA-protein recognition, binding or complexes (incl. RNA-binding proteins, complex structures) Covers the former `rna-protein-complex` and `rna-binding-protein`.
RNA secondary structure as the studied entity.
RNA recognition motif domain (most common RNA-binding domain).
Synonymous mutation class (not individual point mutations).
BIPA database of protein-nucleic acid interactions in 3D structures.
Protein-RNA docking benchmark sets used for training or evaluation.
RNAct database of predicted and experimental protein-RNA interactions.
World Wide Protein Data Bank structures as the data source.
Cancer/tumour disease class as a studied context (disease annotations, cancer cell lines). Not a molecular target (bio:) or therapy (app:).
tags.components: atomic; pair with a bio: entity or data: resource

tags.definition: Predicting binding strength (e.g. ΔG, Kd). Not residue-level.
tags.components: atomic; pair with an ml: model

tags.definition: Identifying binding residues or sites (residue/site-level). Covers former `binding-site-identification`.
Scanning sequences for known binding sites or motifs.
Buried surface area analysis of interfaces.
CEST NMR for sparsely populated conformational states. Stack with `met:nmr`.
CLIP-seq family of crosslinking assays (use `met:eclip` for eCLIP specifically).
Evolutionary/conservation-rate analysis of proteins or interfaces.
Selecting predictive features for a model.
Analysis of hydrogen bonds in structures.
Predicting whether or which molecules interact. Not affinity (`met:binding-affinity-prediction`) or residue-level (`met:binding-residue-prediction`).
tags.components: atomic; pair with a bio:*-interaction tag

tags.definition: Analysis of molecular interface properties (size, composition, contacts).
Metainference integration of experimental data into MD.
Assessing the effect of point mutations.
Parallel analysis of RNA structure (PARS) probing.
Peak calling on sequencing-based binding data.
Comparing existing predictors on common data.
RNA maps: positional distribution of peaks around landmarks.
Predicting functional or interaction motifs in RNA sequences.
Scoring/energy functions for ranking structures. Always `met:`, never `tool:`.
Predictions from sequence only (no structure input).
Use of Boltzmann ensembles of RNA structures.
Deep learning in general; use a specific architecture tag (`ml:cnn`) when one exists.

tags.components: atomic; pair with a specific architecture

tags.definition: Integrated Gradients attribution for model interpretation.
Generic regression model; use a specific model tag if there is one.
Chaperone-assisted folding of RNA or proteins as a process. The chaperone itself is bio:molecular-chaperone.
Conformational change, plasticity or dynamics of a biomolecule (e.g. upon binding) as a natural process. The method used to study it is met: (met:molecular-dynamics, met:cest-nmr).
Folding of disordered regions upon binding.
Translation of RNA into protein (incl. small ORF translation of lncRNAs) as the biological process studied. The assay is met:ribosome-profiling.
tags.components: atomic; pair with met:ribosome-profiling or bio:mrna

tags.definition: PredPRBA web server for protein-RNA binding affinity.
PRI HotScore web server for protein-RNA hotspot scoring.
RBPSignal tool/web server for RBP binding signals.
RegRNA 3.0 RNA motif analysis web server/workflow.
